email.body1:
Mark, saw Nextech rolled out Cora Scribe and an expanded embedded payments platform this year.

When the product surface grows that fast, business development usually has more specialty practices worth touching than the team can actually cover, and that is where pipeline leaks. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Nextech off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Mark, quick follow-up for Nextech.

After a product expansion, the list of accounts in play tends to balloon past what reps can work, so most teams cannot say how many meetings they actually need to hit target. The gap shows up late, and by then the quarter is a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Nextech needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Mark, last bit of proof for Nextech.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Nextech's reply rate likely compares to other healthcare-software teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Mark, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Right after a product launch, timing is everything, and the rollout-to-revenue stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a specialty healthcare motion? I will tailor it to Nextech either way.
